notes.meaning: A good reputation and the kind regard of others are worth far more than silver and gold. Money cannot buy true respect or character, and wealth soon passes away while a good name endures. When people respect our character, we are also better able to honor God and help others.

Rich and poor people live side by side in society, and the Lord created every one of them. God sets each person's earthly lot, so the wealthy should never look down on the poor, and the poor should not envy the rich. Before God's throne of grace and at His final judgment, all people stand on equal ground.

A wise person senses danger or temptation ahead and quickly steps out of harm's way. Foolish and careless people ignore the warnings, rush blindly forward, and end up paying a heavy price. True faith flees to God for safety before judgment falls.

Showing humility before God and revering Him brings rich blessings. While God often provides for our needs in this life, the greatest rewards are spiritual honor, peace, and eternal life. Walking humbly with God is the foundation of a truly blessed life.

The path of crooked and rebellious people is covered with painful thorns and hidden traps. Their stubborn sins bring them constant trouble and grief. A person who guards his soul stays far away from evil paths and walks in safety.

Parents are called to dedicate their children to God early and guide them in the right way of wisdom. Good habits and godly lessons formed in childhood sink deep into the heart. When those children grow old, that early teaching will stay with them and help keep them on the right path.

differ.view: Believes that if parents faithfully train their child in God's ways, God promises the child will never depart from the path of life.
Views this as a general rule and duty rather than an absolute promise, knowing children still have their own wills and some may wander.
Teaches this is a wise principle about parenting rather than an unconditional guarantee, since a youth's choices also shape their future.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many scholars read 'his way' as referring to a child's natural abilities or stage of development, meaning education should fit the child's individual traits.

notes.meaning: In this world, wealth gives people power over the poor, and borrowers fall under the power of those who lend to them. Debt creates a burden of dependence that feels like slavery. Wise people strive to live within their means and stay free from unnecessary debt.

Anyone who plants seeds of injustice and cruelty will harvest trouble and ruin for himself. A bully's power to hurt others will not last forever. God will break the rod of his fury and bring his tyranny to an end.

A generous person who looks with compassion on the needy will receive God's blessing. Such a person is willing to share his own food with those who have nothing. God honors this kindness and replenishes the one who cares for the poor.

Mockers who treat serious things lightly and insult others constantly stir up quarrels. If you remove the troublemaker from the group, the arguing and disgrace come to an end. Peace returns when disrespectful speech is not allowed to fester.

A person with an honest heart and gracious speech makes a valuable friend and advisor. Earthly rulers value servants whose motives are clean and whose words are respectful. Even more, the King of kings befriends those whose hearts are sincere and pure.

The Lord watches over and protects true knowledge and the people who uphold it. At the same time, He ruins the plans and deceitful words of unfaithful men. No scheme against God's truth will ever succeed.

A lazy person invents wild and ridiculous excuses to avoid doing any real work. He claims there is a deadly lion lurking in the street, pretending that duty is too dangerous. In reality, he only makes up stories to comfort his guilty conscience and stay in bed.

The seductive speech of an immoral woman is like a deep, hidden pit designed to trap the unwary. Falling into such sexual sin shows that a person has turned from God and is suffering the consequences of his rebellion. It is a dangerous trap that is very hard to escape.

Children are born with foolishness and sinful habits bound tightly in their hearts. Loving and firm discipline is needed to correct bad behavior and steer them toward wisdom. Left to themselves, children will not outgrow their foolish nature without guided correction.

Taking advantage of the poor to get rich and bribing the wealthy to win favor both lead to poverty. God is deeply offended when the helpless are cheated, and wasting money to flatter the powerful brings no lasting reward. In the end, selfish schemes leave a person empty-handed.

The teacher calls on the listener to pay close attention and store up wise teaching in his inner heart. Keeping these truths in mind brings genuine delight and peace. It also prepares a person to speak with wisdom and grace whenever others need guidance.

The main goal of all this instruction is to lead the listener to put his full trust in the Lord. Wisdom is taught directly and personally to each individual so that faith becomes real and active. True religion is built on depending upon God every day.

The teacher reminds his student that he has written down valuable, trustworthy sayings filled with sound counsel. These words are meant to give solid assurance about what is true and right. They equip the learner to give clear, truthful answers to those who ask him for advice.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Many modern scholars translate the phrase as 'thirty sayings' and note that this section shares a structure and themes with the ancient Egyptian collection known as the Instruction of Amenemope.

notes.meaning: It is a terrible sin to cheat the poor or deny justice to the weak in the city gates where legal matters are decided. Because the helpless have no power of their own, the Lord Himself steps in as their Defender. God will take up their cause and bring ruin on those who mistreat them.

Do not make close friends with someone who has a quick temper and easily loses control. Spending time with angry people is contagious, and you will soon pick up their bad habits. Becoming hot-headed yourself will trap your soul in sin and trouble.

A person should never rashly guarantee someone else's debt by striking hands in agreement. If you promise to pay money you do not have, the lender may come and seize even the bed you sleep on. It is foolish and irresponsible to put your family's basic security at risk for another person's debts.

Ancient boundary stones marked property lines that had been settled for generations, and they were never to be moved. Shifting a marker was a dishonest attempt to steal land from a neighbor. God commands His people to respect other people's property and uphold longstanding rights.

A person who works hard and masters his craft will eventually rise to places of honor. Instead of remaining in obscurity, his skill will open doors to serve kings and leaders. Diligence brings respect in this life, and being faithful in God's service prepares us to stand before the King of kings.
